pages.text: At 9 p.m., Lamiokor’s phone buzzed. A voice note had been forwarded in the JHS 2 class group: ‘Urgent! School closes tomorrow because of a serious outbreak. Forward to everyone you know!’ The voice sounded official, but nobody said who had recorded it.
sentences: A voice note had been forwarded in the JHS 2 class group: ‘Urgent!
School closes tomorrow because of a serious outbreak.
Forward to everyone you know!’ The voice sounded official, but nobody said who had recorded it.
pages.alt: A girl sits on her bed reading a message on her phone with a worried look.

pages.text: Within minutes, the group exploded. ‘I am not going!’ ‘Mum says keep us home!’ Prince had already forwarded it to three other groups. Lamiokor felt a knot in her stomach. ‘Wait,’ she typed. ‘Who actually said this?’
sentences: ‘I am not going!’ ‘Mum says keep us home!’ Prince had already forwarded it to three other groups.
Lamiokor felt a knot in her stomach.
pages.alt: Phone screens show a fast-moving class chat; one girl types a careful message.

pages.text: She listened again, slowly, and wrote down what she noticed. No name. No date. No school name. No phone number to call. And the message demanded urgent forwarding, which can make people share before they think.
sentences: She listened again, slowly, and wrote down what she noticed.
And the message demanded urgent forwarding, which can make people share before they think.
pages.alt: The girl writes a short list in her exercise book next to her phone.

pages.text: Prince looked embarrassed. ‘But what if it is true?’ ‘Then we will find out properly,’ said Lamiokor. ‘Three questions. Who said it? Can another trusted source confirm it? Is it trying to make us panic?’
sentences: ‘But what if it is true?’ ‘Then we will find out properly,’ said Lamiokor.
Can another trusted source confirm it?
Is it trying to make us panic?’
pages.alt: Two classmates talk on a school corridor, one holding up three fingers.

pages.text: It was too late to call the school office, so Lamiokor messaged the class prefect, who agreed to ask the headteacher in the morning. She also asked the group to pause forwarding until they knew more. Some did. Some did not.
sentences: It was too late to call the school office, so Lamiokor messaged the class prefect, who agreed to ask the headteacher in the morning.
She also asked the group to pause forwarding until they knew more.
pages.alt: The girl types to the class prefect while a pause icon is shown on the group chat.

pages.text: Next morning, a notice appeared on the school gate, signed and dated by the headteacher with a phone number: ‘School is open as normal. A voice note is circulating that did not come from the school. Please do not forward it.’
sentences: Next morning, a notice appeared on the school gate, signed and dated by the headteacher with a phone number: ‘School is open as normal.
A voice note is circulating that did not come from the school.
pages.alt: Students gather at a school gate to read a notice taped to the wall.

pages.text: Prince apologised in the group. ‘I shared it too fast. I did not mean to scare anyone.’ ‘Most of us did the same,’ said Lamiokor. ‘The trick is to pause before pressing forward.’
sentences: I did not mean to scare anyone.’ ‘Most of us did the same,’ said Lamiokor.
‘The trick is to pause before pressing forward.’
pages.alt: The boy speaks quietly to a small group of classmates; the girl listens and nods.

pages.text: The class made a poster for the noticeboard: STOP. Who said it? Can I confirm it? Does it want me to panic? Then decide. ‘Everyone makes mistakes,’ said Lamiokor. ‘Checking is how we fix them.’ The end.
sentences: The class made a poster for the noticeboard: STOP.
Does it want me to panic?
‘Checking is how we fix them.’ The end.
pages.alt: Students pin a hand-drawn poster with bold words to a school noticeboard.

activities.question: Which detail made Lamiokor doubt the voice note?
options: It had no name, date or contact number, and demanded quick forwarding

activities.prompt: Lamiokor cannot reach the school office tonight. What could she do to check the message?
options: Ask someone who can reach the headteacher

activities.question: What made the notice at the gate more trustworthy than the voice note?
options: It was signed and dated and had a phone number

activities.definition: Being passed from person to person.

activities.prompt: Put the steps Lamiokor took in order.
items: Noticed what was missing from the message.
Asked three questions about the source.
Asked someone who could check with the school.

activities.prompt: Prince felt embarrassed after sharing too fast. When have you shared something before checking it? How could you handle it kindly next time?

glossary.definition: A sudden rise in cases of an illness or other problem.
Being passed from person to person.
Sending on a message you received to other people.
